newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Kia chairman refuses to resign unconditionally.
newsitem.headline: Kia chairman refuses to resign unconditionally.

text.p: The head of the troubled Kia Group said on Friday he would not accept the demand by creditor banks that he resign unconditionally in exchange for a bailout.
"I cannot accept creditors' demand for my unconditional resignation," chairman Kim Sun-hong told reporters after a meeting of creditors.
He also said he would not sell off the group's commercial vehicle unit Asia Motors.
"Integrating Asia Motors into Kia Motors after selling some assets is the most rational thing to do," Kim said.
Creditors have been pressing for the resignation of the chairman and the sale of Asia Motors as a precondition for extending a bailout programme to the ailing group.

The second meeting of Kia creditors in the afternoon failed to map out the rescue plan because of disagreement on the two core issues, bank officials said. Creditors would meet again on August 4 at 0600 GMT, they said.
